s1.syndrome_frame: Abnormal cardiac conduction and morphology with unusual cardiac positioning
salient_findings: Apex of the heart located at the right side of the chest
Hepatic dullness in the left subcostal region
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 80s
No previous medical records available
Patient denies any history of chest pain
ECG shows wide complex rhythm at rate of 76 beats/min with right bundle branch block morphology
QRS duration of 120 milliseconds
Negative P waves with pathological Q waves in leads I and aVL
Positive P waves in lead V1
Biphasic P waves in leads V2 through V6
Pathological Q waves in leads V5 and V6
Transthoracic Echocardiogram shows right atrium and right ventricle on the left side and left atrium and left ventricle on the right side

raw.champion: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries
raw.rationale: The patient's echocardiogram shows the right atrium and right ventricle on the left side and the left atrium and left ventricle on the right side, which is consistent with congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries. The ECG findings also support this diagnosis, with a wide complex rhythm and right bundle branch block morphology.

rejected.label: Dextrocardia with situs solitus
rejected.why: Dextrocardia would typically show the heart on the right side, but the apex would still be directed to the left, which is not the case here.

rejected.label: Cardiac malposition
rejected.why: Cardiac malposition is a broader term that could encompass several conditions, but it does not specifically explain the unique anatomy seen in this patient's echocardiogram.

rejected.label: Heterotaxy syndrome
rejected.why: Heterotaxy syndrome involves complex abnormalities of the abdominal and thoracic organs, which are not described in this patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Ebstein's anomaly
rejected.why: Ebstein's anomaly involves a specific defect of the tricuspid valve and right ventricle, which is not mentioned in the patient's ECG or echocardiogram findings.
